fit_reason: TSMC makes leading-edge wafers and does CoWoS advanced packaging for nearly every AI accelerator, making it the core foundry and packager in the sub-sector. Both leading-edge wafers and advanced packaging are concentrated at TSMC and slow to add elsewhere, so it holds the scarce capacity that sets how many accelerators can be made. Foundry is its entire business and it is the dominant player by a wide margin.

ASML makes lithography systems, including the only EUV tools in the world, plus metrology and inspection, making it an equipment supplier for leading-edge wafers. Every leading-edge wafer needs its lithography, so it gains directly as foundries add capacity to meet accelerator demand. Lithography is its whole business and it is a monopoly supplier at EUV.

Lam Research makes etch, deposition and wafer cleaning tools, including through-silicon via etch used in advanced packaging and HBM stacking, making it an equipment supplier. More leading-edge wafers and more advanced packaging both require more of its tools, so it gains from the capacity build. Wafer fab equipment is its entire business and it is one of the largest suppliers, a leader in etch.

Applied Materials makes wafer fabrication tools across deposition, etch, implant, CMP and inspection, plus services to fabs, making it an equipment and materials-engineering supplier. Its tools are needed for every new leading-edge wafer and for hybrid bonding and other advanced packaging steps, so it gains from more wafers and packaging. Semiconductor equipment is its whole business and it is the largest and broadest supplier.

KLA makes wafer and reticle inspection, metrology and process control systems, including tools for advanced packaging, making it an equipment supplier. Process control rises with leading-edge complexity and packaging yields, so it gains as foundries and packagers add capacity. Semiconductor process control is nearly all of its business and it is the dominant player in inspection and metrology.

ASE is the largest outside semiconductor packager and tester, offering flip-chip, fan-out wafer-level packaging and 2.5D silicon interposers, making it an outside packager. Advanced packaging is tight and concentrated at TSMC, so outside packagers like ASE gain volume as the alternative and overflow. Packaging and test is its core business and it is the global leader among outside packagers.

Amkor provides outside semiconductor packaging and test, including wafer bumping, flip-chip, fan-out and silicon wafer integrated fan-out, making it an outside packager. Outside packagers gain volume as alternatives to TSMC's tight advanced packaging capacity, and Amkor is building advanced packaging capacity that adds to supply. Packaging and test is its entire business and it is the second-largest outside packager.

ASM International makes single-wafer atomic layer deposition, PECVD, epitaxy and furnace systems, making it an equipment supplier for leading-edge wafers. ALD and epitaxy steps multiply at gate-all-around nodes, so it gains as leading-edge capacity is added for accelerators. Deposition equipment is its whole business and it is the leader in ALD.

Intel runs Intel Foundry, which makes leading-edge wafers and offers advanced packaging, alongside its CPU and GPU businesses, making it a foundry and packager alternative to TSMC. The sub-sector says other foundries gain volume as alternatives because leading-edge capacity is concentrated at TSMC, and Intel is the main Western leading-edge alternative. Foundry is a meaningful but not majority part of its business, and its importance rests on whether outside customers adopt its nodes and packaging.

Qnity supplies electronic materials essential for making semiconductor chips, the business spun out of DuPont, which per what is known includes CMP pads and slurries, photoresist materials and advanced packaging materials, making it a materials supplier. Materials are consumed with every wafer and packaging step, so it gains from more leading-edge wafers and advanced packaging. Semiconductor materials are its whole business, and it is a large supplier, though its description is thin.

Entegris supplies ultra-pure process chemicals, specialty gases, filtration and purification, and wafer handling products to chipmakers, making it a materials supplier. Contamination control matters more at leading-edge nodes, and its consumables scale with wafer volume, so it gains from more wafers. Semiconductor materials are central to its business and it is a leading supplier in microcontamination control.

Onto Innovation makes macro defect inspection, optical metrology and packaging lithography tools, with a strong position in advanced packaging, making it an equipment supplier. Advanced packaging is where capacity is being added fastest, so its packaging inspection and lithography tools gain directly. Process control and packaging tools are its entire business and it is a leading supplier to advanced packaging lines.

Camtek makes 2D and 3D inspection and metrology systems built for advanced packaging, including fan-out and HBM-related interconnects, making it an equipment supplier. Advanced packaging is tight and being expanded, so demand for its inspection tools tracks that buildout. Inspection for advanced packaging is the core of its business and it is a leading specialist there.

Kulicke and Soffa makes semiconductor assembly equipment, including flip-chip and thermo-compression bonding (TCB) tools for advanced packaging, plus ball bonders and consumables, making it an equipment supplier. TCB and flip-chip bonding are used in advanced packaging, which is the tightest constraint on accelerator supply, so it gains as packaging capacity is added. Assembly equipment is its entire business, though much of it still serves mature wire-bonding markets.

Nova makes dimensional, film and chemical metrology used across lithography, etch, CMP, deposition and advanced packaging, making it an equipment supplier. Metrology steps rise with leading-edge complexity and packaging, so it gains as foundries and memory makers add advanced capacity. Process control is its entire business and it is a leading metrology specialist.

Advantest makes automated test systems and handlers for SoC and memory devices, including the testing of accelerators and HBM, used by foundries and outside packagers. Test is part of the back-end alongside advanced packaging, so it gains as more accelerators are made, though the sub-sector names wafers and packaging rather than test, which makes it borderline. Semiconductor test is its core business and it is the largest supplier of SoC test for AI chips.

HOYA makes mask blanks and photomasks for semiconductor production, including EUV mask blanks, alongside a large medical and eyecare business, making it a materials supplier for leading-edge wafers. Every new leading-edge design and lithography layer needs masks, so it gains from more leading-edge wafers. It is a meaningful part of a diversified business and it is a leading supplier of EUV mask blanks.

GlobalFoundries is a semiconductor foundry making wafers on mature and specialty nodes, including silicon photonics, making it a foundry. The sub-sector says other foundries gain volume as alternatives in smaller volumes, but GlobalFoundries does not make leading-edge accelerator wafers, so its share of the growth is limited. Foundry is its entire business and it is a major Western specialty foundry.

UMC is a wafer foundry offering mask generation, wafer manufacturing, assembly and test, making it a foundry. It runs mature nodes, so it gains only indirectly as an alternative foundry rather than from leading-edge accelerator wafers. Foundry is its entire business and it is one of the larger mature-node foundries.

Veeco makes laser annealing, ion beam deposition, MOCVD, ALD, wet processing and packaging lithography tools, making it an equipment supplier. Its laser annealing serves leading-edge logic and its packaging lithography and wet processing serve advanced packaging, both areas that gain from accelerator volume. Semiconductor and thin-film equipment is its whole business, though it is a smaller player than the major tool makers.

Axcelis makes ion implantation systems and services for chip fabrication, making it an equipment supplier. Implant is needed for every wafer, but its business leans to power devices and mature nodes rather than leading-edge accelerator wafers, so its gain from the sub-sector is less direct. Ion implantation is its entire business and it is one of the two main suppliers.

Ultra Clean makes gas and chemical delivery systems, process modules and other subsystems for semiconductor equipment makers, and provides chamber cleaning and contamination analysis, making it an equipment supplier. It gains as tool makers ship more equipment for leading-edge wafers and packaging. Semiconductor equipment subsystems are its core business and it is a leading outsourced subsystem supplier to the major tool makers.

Ichor makes gas and chemical delivery subsystems and precision components for semiconductor etch, deposition, CMP and cleaning tools, making it an equipment supplier. Its sales track the equipment shipments that build leading-edge wafer capacity. Fluid delivery for semiconductor equipment is nearly its whole business, and it is a key subsystem supplier to the largest tool makers.

MKS supplies vacuum, pressure and flow control, RF and microwave power for etch and deposition, lasers and optics for wafer fabrication, and laser systems for PCB and substrate processing, making it an equipment and materials supplier. It gains as tool makers build more equipment for leading-edge wafers and as packaging substrates grow. Semiconductor is a meaningful part of a diversified business and it is a major subsystem supplier.

Advanced Energy makes RF and DC plasma power supplies, matching networks and remote plasma sources used in etch and deposition tools, plus power for other markets, making it an equipment supplier. Plasma power is needed in the tools that make leading-edge wafers, so it gains with equipment shipments. Semiconductor equipment is a meaningful part of its business and it is a leading plasma power supplier.

Teradyne makes semiconductor test systems at wafer and package level, including for compute and memory, alongside robotics and other test businesses. Test sits beside packaging in the back end and grows with accelerator volume, but the sub-sector names wafers and packaging rather than test, so it is borderline. Semiconductor test is the largest part of its business and it is one of the two leading test suppliers.

FormFactor makes probe cards for testing SoCs, GPUs and DRAM at the wafer level, plus probing and metrology systems, making it a test and measurement supplier to foundries and chipmakers. Wafer probing grows with leading-edge wafers and HBM, but test is not named directly in the sub-sector, which makes it borderline. Probe cards are its core business and it is a leading probe card supplier.

Photronics makes photomasks that transfer circuit patterns onto wafers and display substrates, making it a materials supplier. Every new chip design needs masks, but Photronics serves mostly mature and mainstream nodes, so its link to leading-edge accelerator wafers is limited. Photomasks are its whole business and it is a leading merchant supplier.

ACM Research makes single-wafer wet cleaning systems and electro-chemical plating tools for chip fabrication, making it an equipment supplier. Cleaning and plating are needed for more wafers and for advanced packaging, but its customers are largely in mainland China rather than at the leading-edge foundries building for accelerators. Wafer equipment is its entire business and it is a smaller player.

Tower is a specialty foundry offering SiGe, BiCMOS, RF CMOS, image sensors, power and silicon photonics processes, making it a foundry. It does not make leading-edge accelerator wafers, so it gains from the sub-sector only as a smaller alternative foundry. Foundry is its entire business and it is a leading specialty analog foundry.

Element Solutions supplies specialty chemicals for electronics, including wafer bumping, die attach, copper interconnect and photomask solutions for IC fabrication and semiconductor packaging, making it a materials supplier. Packaging chemistries are consumed as advanced packaging grows, so it gains from packaging volume. Electronics is a meaningful part of its business, with packaging chemistries a modest slice of it.

Materion makes vapor deposition targets, microelectronics packaging materials and precision optics used in semiconductor fabrication, along with alloys for other industries, making it a materials supplier. Deposition targets are consumed with each wafer, so it gains from more wafers. Semiconductor materials are a meaningful part of a diversified business.

Cohu makes semiconductor test handlers, contactors, probe heads and wafer-level and package test equipment, used by chipmakers and outside packagers. Test grows with chip volume, but the sub-sector names wafers and packaging rather than test, and much of Cohu's business serves automotive and mobile chips. Back-end test is its core business but it is a smaller player.

Aehr makes wafer-level and die-level burn-in and test systems with full-wafer contactors for logic, memory and photonic devices. Wafer-level burn-in can serve AI processors and packaged modules, but it is test rather than wafers or packaging, so it is borderline. Burn-in is its entire business, and it is a small player.

ChipMOS provides outside assembly, test, wafer probing and bumping, mainly for memory and display driver chips, making it an outside packager. It works with leadframe and organic substrate packages rather than the advanced packaging that limits accelerator supply, so its gain from the sub-sector is small. Packaging and test is its entire business but it is a small, legacy-focused player.

PDF Solutions sells yield and manufacturing analytics software, process control, test and assembly data tools and e-beam characterization used by foundries, chipmakers and outside packagers. It supports the making of wafers and packaging, but it sells software rather than equipment or materials, so it is borderline. Semiconductor manufacturing is its whole market, and it is a niche player.

EnPro provides cleaning, coating, refurbishment and testing for semiconductor equipment components through its Advanced Surface Technologies segment, plus seals used in semiconductor fabrication, making it an equipment-related supplier. These services grow with the installed base of fab tools, so it gains as wafer capacity is added. Semiconductor is a meaningful part of a diversified industrial business.

Coherent makes lasers, laser-based systems and optics used in microelectronics fabrication, alongside many other laser applications. Lasers are used in some wafer and packaging steps, so it gains somewhat from more capacity, but the link is indirect and borderline. Microelectronics is one of several markets for its lasers.

Corning makes glass wafers and substrates and optics and consumables for semiconductor equipment, among much larger optical fiber, display and other businesses. Glass carriers and equipment optics are used in wafer and packaging steps, so it gains somewhat from more capacity, but this is borderline. Semiconductor is a small part of its business.

Benchmark Electronics is a contract manufacturer whose customers include semiconductor capital equipment makers, for which it builds and tests subsystems. It gains when tool makers ship more equipment for wafer and packaging capacity, but it is a manufacturing services provider rather than an equipment supplier, which makes it borderline. Semiconductor capital equipment is one of its several markets.

DuPont's description includes materials for semiconductor front-end and back-end processes and advanced packaging, which would make it a materials supplier. Per what is known, that electronics business has been separated into Qnity, which is listed separately, so the remaining DuPont's exposure is likely small. It is kept as borderline on the strength of its description only.
